source.title: Open problems for the superKdV equations

accepted.question_text: For supersymmetric extensions of the KdV equation with an odd Poisson structure, are there further integrable odd extensions in which the bosonic fields do couple to the fermionic fields in their time-evolution equations, rather than decoupling from them?

evidence.quote: A new N = 2 super KdV equation with an odd Poisson structure has been found recently in [7] but the resulting equations are somewhat less interesting in that the bosonic fields do not couple to the fermions in their time evolution. It would be of interest to see whether there are other ‘odd’ integrable extensions displaying fermionic interactions in the bosonic evolution equations.

accepted.question_text: For the N = 1 supersymmetric KdV equation with Lax operator L = ∂^2 − φD and fermionic nonlocal conservation laws J_{k/2} = ∫ dxdθ sRes L^{k/4} for odd k, find an integrable deformation that reproduces this family of fermionic nonlocal conservation laws.

evidence.quote: The fermionic nonlocal conservation laws are thus related to the super residues of the fourth root of odd powers of the Lax operators as Jk/2 = ∫ dxdθ sResLk/4 (k odd) (2.26)
OP-1: Find an integrable deformation that reproduces the fermionic nonlocal conservation laws.

accepted.question_text: For the N = 2 supersymmetric KdV family SKdV_a, which is integrable exactly for a = −2, 1, 4 and has infinitely many conservation laws obtained from the corresponding Lax operators, find an integrable deformation for SKdV_{−2}, SKdV_1, and SKdV_4 that reproduces their conservation laws.

evidence.quote: This is called the SKdVa equation (the capital S is used for N = 2). This system is integrable for exactly three values of a [3]: a = −2, 1, 4 .

Although there exists a Miura transformation, there are no known integrable (i.e., Gardner-type) deformations of it. This leads us to: OP-2: Find an integrable deformation for SKdV−2,1,4 that reproduces their conservations laws.

accepted.question_text: For the integrable N = 2 equations SKdV_{−2} and SKdV_4, which each possess two independent towers of fermionic nonlocal conservation laws and whose Lax operators have two distinct fourth roots, determine how those fermionic nonlocal conservation laws are related to the Lax operator.
accepted.context_brief: Lax origin of N=2 fermionic laws

evidence.quote: For a = −2, 4, there are two independent towers of fermionic nonlocal conservations laws [18]

However, although the Lax operator has two distinct fourth roots, these have not yet been related to these fermionic conservation laws: OP-3: For SKdV−2,4, find the relation between the fermionic nonlocal conservation laws and the Lax operator.

accepted.question_text: For the integrable N = 2 equation SKdV_1, why do the first fermionic conservation laws fail to generate infinite towers of fermionic nonlocal conservation laws, unlike the a = −2 and a = 4 cases?

evidence.quote: On the other hand, for the a = 1 case, the first fermionic laws (3.9) do not generate infinite towers: they are isolated.
OP-4: Why there are no infinite towers of fermionic conservation laws for SKdV1?

accepted.question_text: Is the integrable N = 2 equation SKdV_1 bihamiltonian?

evidence.quote: In that respect, the SKdV1 stands as one of the rare example of classical integrable system which is not (known to be) bihamiltonian.

accepted.question_text: Why are there exactly three integrable N = 2 super KdV extensions, namely the cases a = −2, 1, and 4, and is there an underlying Lie-algebraic explanation for this threefold classification?
accepted.context_brief: Why exactly three integrable N=2 cases

evidence.quote: This system is integrable for exactly three values of a [3]: a = −2, 1, 4 .

OP-6: Why is there exactly three integrable N = 2 super KdV extensions?14 Is there an underlying Lie algebraic interpretation for this threefold way (i.e, is this related to the existence of the three classical algebras)?

accepted.question_text: Is it possible to formulate the Painlevé analysis directly in superspace for super integrable systems such as the supersymmetric KdV equations?

evidence.quote: As stressed here, these equations are naturally formulated in superspace. Over the years, it became clear that a lot of structure is contained in the Painlev´e test: for instance its truncation leads to Backl¨und transformations and the Lax operator [20]. Yet, no Painlev´e analysis has been done directly in superspace.
OP-7: Is it possible to formulate the Painlev´e analysis in superspace?

accepted.question_text: For the N = 2 supersymmetric KdV equations, can one construct or characterize Darboux transformations analogous to the N = 1 case?

evidence.quote: The Darboux transformation in the N = 1 case has been worked out in [21] but nothing has been done at this point concerning the N = 2 cases.

needs_review.question_text_raw: little is known on the super version of the connection between geometry and soliton theory; the super KdV equations have super Sine-Gordon relatives that should lead to interesting geometrical structures

evidence.quote: Finally, unravelling the deep relations between geometry and soliton theory has been an important theme of this workshop; little is known on the super version of this connection. In particular, the super KdV equations have super Sine-Gordon relatives and these should lead to very interesting geometrical structures.
